newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Mogas extends losses.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Mogas extends losses.

text.p: Taiwan issued an import tender for reformate for May and June arrival as gasoline prices in Singapore extended its losses.

Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp's (CPC) tender which closes April 21 and is valid for two days, seeks a 250,000-barrel cargo of unleaded reformate for delivery in May 16-31 and/or June 1-15 and a 250,000-barrel cargo of leaded reformate for June 1-15 arrival.

In its last tender for its May 1-15 requirements, CPC bought two unleaded cargoes at $27.40 per barrel, c-and-f, from South Korean refiner Yukong and Dutch trader Vitol, and an unleaded cargo from Swiss trader Glencore at $27.70.
A CPC official said it issued a tender for the two delivery timings as it may need two unleaded cargoes.
"They might as well since it (gasoline) is under pressure," said a trader.
Fob Singapore gasoline prices extended its losses as majors failed to attract buyers with their aggressive offers.
Naphtha swaps edged up slightly with crude with May swaps last quoted at $21.60/$21.80 per barrel, from $21.50/$21.60 on Friday.
Physical talk was thin but weak demand was pressuring down premiums for fob Singapore barrels to less than 50 cents per barrel, traders said.
